name: Question 3
problem: A curve has parametric equations $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+4,\,y=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{9}.$
worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+4)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t))}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =\frac{12{sec}^{2}⁡(3t)}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =4{sec}^{3}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\frac{\pi }{9},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}{|}_{t=\pi /9} & =4{sec}^{3}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{9}) \\  & =\frac{4}{{cos}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{4}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}} \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

A curve has parametric equations x=sin⁡(3t)+4,y=−4cos⁡(3t). Given that dydx=4tan⁡(3t), calculate d2ydx2 at the point where t=π9.

a
132
b
18
c
32
d
8
e
12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute d2ydx2, we can use the formula

d2ydx2=ddt(dydx)(dxdt).

We're given that dydx=4tan⁡(3t), and we can calculate dxdt as follows:

dxdt=ddt(sin⁡(3t)+4)=3cos⁡(3t).

Substituting into the formula, we get

d2ydx2=ddt(4tan⁡(3t))3cos⁡(3t)=12sec2⁡(3t)3cos⁡(3t)=4sec3⁡(3t).

Finally, we evaluate at t=π9, and we get

d2ydx2|t=π/9=4sec3⁡(3⋅π9)=4cos3⁡(π3)=4(12)3=32.
